description: An Arduino with the Uno's shape and pin layout, built around the ATmega32U4 — which has USB built in, so it can pretend to be a mouse or a keyboard.
how_to_use: Same headers as the Uno (digital 0–13, A0–A5, 5V, 3.3V, GND). Plug in with a micro-USB cable. With Mouse.h / Keyboard.h it appears to your computer as a USB mouse or keyboard. Note: its I2C pins are 2 (SDA) and 3 (SCL), not A4/A5.

plain.what: An Arduino that can pretend to be a USB mouse or keyboard for your computer.
plain.how: Wire it just like an Uno (same pins in the same places) and plug it in with a micro-USB cable. Its code can then move your mouse or type.
